questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The book, B. which you recommended, C. was interesting and D. an easily read.
questions.solution: After 'was interesting and', the phrase must be a parallel adjective, not an article + adverb + noun: 'an easily read' is ungrammatical here (it should be 'easy to read'). The error lies in part D. **Answer: an easily read**
questions.shortcut: After 'interesting and', a parallel adjective is expected — 'an' is the giveaway.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:

He neither attended the seminar ___________submitted his report on time.
questions.solution: 'Neither' is always paired with 'nor' as a correlative conjunction: he neither attended... nor submitted... **Answer: nor**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Idiosyncrasy
questions.solution: Idiosyncrasy means an odd or distinctive habit peculiar to an individual, i.e. a peculiarity; commonalty, normality and conformity are opposites. **Answer: Peculiarity**
questions.shortcut: Idio- (own, personal) → something personal and peculiar.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:

The politician's speech was full of vague promises but ultimately it was just________.
questions.solution: 'Smoke and mirrors' denotes deliberate deception and concealment of the truth through misleading presentation — apt for a speech of vague promises. 'A red herring' is a misleading side issue, not deceptive showmanship. **Answer: smoke and mirrors**
questions.shortcut: Vague promises + hiding the truth → smoke and mirrors.

questions.q: Which of the following sentences uses the word "wave" with the same meaning as in the "She gave a friendly wave to her neighbor"
options: The dog loved to chase the waves on the beach.
The crowd gave a slow wave as the parade passed by.
The ocean waves crashed against the shore.
questions.solution: In the given sentence 'wave' means a gesture of greeting with the hand. 'The crowd gave a slow wave as the parade passed by' uses the same sense; the other sentences use wave = a swell of water. **Answer: The crowd gave a slow wave as the parade passed by.**
questions.shortcut: Match the part of speech: 'gave a wave' is a hand gesture, so look for the sentence where wave is also an action of greeting.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'Effervescence' — e-f-f-e-r-v-e-s-c-e-n-c-e (bubbling fizz, or lively enthusiasm). **Answer: Effervescence**
questions.shortcut: Remember the stem 'fervesce' (from Latin fervescere); no extra 's' or 'a'.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.solution: 'Personnel' with a double 'n' is correct — it means the staff or employees of an organisation. **Answer: Personnel**
questions.shortcut: Personnel = persons ⇒ double 'n' like double 'p' in 'person-to-person'.

questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Whatever floats your boat
options: Something that is easy to do
questions.solution: 'Whatever floats your boat' means whatever pleases or suits you — said to accept another person's preference. **Answer: Something that makes you happy**

questions.q: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: A person who loves and collects stamps
questions.solution: A philatelist collects and studies postage stamps; a numismatist collects coins, and a bibliophile loves books. **Answer: Philatelist**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Serene
questions.solution: Serene means calm, peaceful and untroubled; its opposite is chaotic. Calm, peaceful and tranquil are synonyms, not antonyms. **Answer: Chaotic**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Sagacious
questions.solution: Sagacious means having keen mental discernment and sound judgement, i.e. wise. Prudent is close but stresses caution, while 'wise' is the direct synonym. **Answer: Wise**

questions.q:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A belief that the Earth is the center of the universe
questions.solution: 'Geo' = earth, so geocentrism is the belief that the Earth is the centre of the universe; heliocentrism places the Sun at the centre. **Answer: Geocentrism**
questions.shortcut: geo = earth, helio = sun — the prefix settles it.

questions.q:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Let the documents be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
options: You should submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
The documents will be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Let the head of the department submit the documents by the end of the week.
questions.solution: 'Let + object + be + past participle' is the passive form of an imperative sentence. Its active form is the plain imperative: 'Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.' **Answer: Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.**
questions.shortcut: 'Let ... be + V3' in passive ⇔ plain imperative in active.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The librarian told the child, "You should not be making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams."
options: The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he should not have been making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he would not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams.
questions.solution: In indirect speech 'should' does not change, but the present perfect continuous 'have been trying' backshifts to 'had been trying' — exactly option A. **Answer: The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.**
questions.shortcut: Modal 'should' stays; only present perfect tenses backshift to past perfect.

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

This is __the most toughest exam __that I have ever taken.
questions.solution: 'Most toughest' is a double superlative — the superlative of 'tough' is simply 'toughest'. **Answer: the toughest exam**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The fraud comes at a time when the unregulated finance industry is facing a crisis **on its way of **high-interest rates and low repayment of loans.
questions.solution: The phrase needed means 'in the form of / when it comes to': the industry is facing a crisis in the way of high interest rates and low repayment of loans. 'On its way of' is unidiomatic, and the other options do not fit grammatically. **Answer: in the way of**

questions.q:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

They had not closed the shop.
options: The shop has not been closed by them.
The shop was not closed by them..
The shop had not been closed by them.
The shop is not closed by them.
questions.solution: Past perfect active 'had not closed' becomes passive 'had not been closed': The shop had not been closed by them. **Answer: The shop had not been closed by them.**
questions.shortcut: had + V3 ⇒ passive needs 'had been + V3' — keep the same tense.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

He said that if he were to receive a promotion, he would buy his family a bigger house.
options: He said, "If I received a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I were to receive a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I receive a promotion, I will buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I had received a promotion, I would have bought my family a bigger house."
questions.solution: Reverting the reported second conditional: 'he' → 'I' while keeping the subjunctive 'were to receive' and 'would buy'. **Answer: He said, "If I were to receive a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."**
questions.shortcut: 'If he were to... , he would...' back to direct = 'If I were to... , I would...'

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He started assembling the deck planks, fastening each one in a neat, even line.

Q. He made sure that every angle was precisely square when he constructed the deck with beams and joists.

R. He prepared the foundation by excavating holes and positioning the building's columns.

S. He took a step back and admired the new outdoor area, a sturdy deck that was made to stay.
questions.solution: The construction follows a natural sequence: foundation and columns (R) → beams and joists (Q) → deck planks (P) → admiring the finished deck (S). **Answer: R, Q, P, S**
questions.shortcut: Build bottom-up: foundation → frame → planks → admire.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. The method, which is titled the Socratic method, is a cornerstone of Western philosophy.

Q. Socrates believed that the path to knowledge was not through lecturing but through a systematic process of questioning.

R. He would probe his students mercilessly, taking them through a chain of logical conclusions.

S. Its goal was not to provide answers but to force the individual to discover the truth for themselves.
questions.solution: Q states Socrates' belief in learning through questioning; P names the method ('the Socratic method'); R describes his probing practice; S concludes with the method's goal ('Its goal...'). **Answer: Q, P, R, S**
questions.shortcut: Chain: belief (Q) → name of method (P) → his practice (R) → its goal (S).
